item.research_question: What are the strength and deformation mechanisms of nanocrystalline Al0.3CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy thin films (HEATFs) compared to bulk samples?
item.processing_route: Magnetron sputtering deposition on silicon wafer substrates; target cleaned by argon ion bombardment for ~2 min; substrate rotation speed 2 rpm; film thickness ~4 μm; nanopillars (diameter 738 nm) fabricated by FIB at 30 kV/10 pA
item.test_conditions: Room temperature; nanoindentation with Berkovich tip (depth <10% of film thickness); in situ SEM compression using flat punch diamond tip at strain rate ~5×10-3 s-1
key_findings: Surface roughness Ra is less than 5 nm (specifically <3.5 nm in some profiles).
Grain size is approximately 10 nm with a homogeneous chemical composition.
Main phase is face-centered cubic (FCC) with a minor ordered BCC NiAl type phase.
Hardness is approximately 11.09 GPa, which is about three times that of bulk samples.
Elastic modulus is approximately 186.01 GPa, nearly the same as bulk samples.
Yield strength of nanopillars is approximately 1024 MPa, about three times that of bulk samples.
Compressive strength reached ~2075 MPa at a strain of ~11.39% before softening.
Plastic deformation is inhomogeneous and localized, occurring first at the top of the pillar.
item.mechanism: The enhanced hardness is ascribed to the nanocrystalline strengthening mechanism induced by a large number of grain boundaries. The inhomogeneous plastic deformation is characterized by localized metal flow and slip generation at the top of the nanopillar.
item.limitations: The text notes that a rigorous diffraction-intensity-distribution calculation of the solid solution phases responsible for certain orientations is beyond the scope of this work.
item.future_work: The results could provide an in-depth understanding of the mechanics and deformation mechanism for future design of nanocrystalline HEATFs with desired properties.
quotes: The hardness and the yield strength of the high-entropy alloy thin film was about three times that of the bulk samples
It indicates that the deformation of the Al0.3CoCrFeNi HEA nanopillar was inhomogeneous
